headlines.article_text: Lululemon poaches Athleta CEO Maggie Gauger as chief product officer Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Lululemon announced Wednesday that Athleta CEO Maggie Gauger has joined the company as its chief product officer, a newly created role. The announcement comes just a month after Heidi O'Neill took over the company as CEO. Athleta owner Gap told CNBC in a statement that the leadership transition will allow it to accelerate its work in repositioning the brand for growth. In this article LULU GAP Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Shoppers enter a Lululemon store in Walnut Creek, California, US, on Wednesday, July 15, 2026. David Paul Morris | Bloomberg | Getty Images Lululemon announced Wednesday that Athleta CEO Maggie Gauger has joined the company as president and chief product officer, effective later this month. The move marks the latest shakeup among the top executives in the increasingly competitive athleisure space: Gauger joined Athleta from Nike only last year. Lululemon said Gauger's job is a newly created role. It also appointed Joseph Godsey as chief operating officer. Alongside the new announcements, Lululemon also said Nikki Neuburger, the company's chief brand and product activation officer, and Ted Dagnese, its chief supply chain officer, are leaving to "pursue other opportunities" in November. "We are establishing a deeply experienced leadership team that will work in a more coordinated manner, aligned around the strategy and execution that delivers the most impact for our guests, our communities, and our business," Lululemon CEO Heidi O'Neill said in a statement. "That starts with putting product, design, and innovation at the center of how we operate, with the focus and accountability to create a stronger pipeline of differentiated product to raise the bar for our guests across every touchpoint, in stores and online." In a statement provided to CNBC, Athleta parent company Gap confirmed Gauger has left the company. It said Erika Everett, the brand's current chief marketing officer, will oversee the brand CEO role in the interim. "We have been actively shaping Athleta's next chapter and the changes needed to position the brand for long-term growth," Gap said in its statement. "This transition enables us to accelerate that work, strengthen our connection with customers, and unlock Athleta's full potential." Separately, Lululemon said it is also searching for a chief brand officer, a chief communications officer and a chief technology officer. O'Neill took the helm of Lululemon last month after the athleisure company saw more than a year of disappointing sales performance in the midst of a proxy battle, drawing criticism from founder Chip Wilson. headlines.summary: The new device shows Microsoft remains committed to making its own PCs even though it's not one of the top device makers.
headlines.article_text: Microsoft starts taking preorders for $2,599 Surface Laptop Ultra Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Microsoft's Surface Laptop Ultra contains an Nvidia chip that can run large AI models without generating cloud bills. The device contains a magnetic USB-C port similar to Apple's MagSafe charging connector. Microsoft also said that Meta will introduce its Muse AI agent for Windows. In this article MSFT Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Microsoft Windows Surface Laptop Ultra. Source: Microsoft Microsoft said its new laptop containing an Nvidia AI chip will start at $2,599, as the software maker tries to bring more artificial intelligence capabilities to its consumer devices. The Surface Laptop Ultra is now available on preorder and will begin shipping on Oct. 16, Pavan Davuluri, Microsoft's executive vice president of Windows and devices, said at a company event in San Francisco on Wednesday. The computer has the world's first magnetic USB-C port, similar to Apple's MagSafe charging connector, along with two other standard USB-C ports, Microsoft said in a blog post . While Microsoft Windows is the most popular operating system for PCs, the company isn't among the top six PC vendors in terms of unit shipments, according to an estimate from researcher Gartner. As the AI boom matures and chip technology advances, tech giants including Microsoft, Apple and Google are aiming to allow users to run more AI workloads from their devices rather than relying on the cloud. Users can install and run a variety of models on the new laptop without having to worry about racking up high monthly bills. Microsoft first talked about the Surface Laptop Ultra in May, but is just now providing specifics. "Microsoft might get me back to Windows," Max Weinbach, an analyst at Creative Strategies, wrote on X after the announcement. Davuluri also said that Meta will introduce a version of its popular Muse AI agent for Windows, capitalizing on the surging popularity of the personal agent, which has jumped to the top of Apple's App store, surpassing ChatGPT. Microsoft is still trying to solidify its role as a key player in AI. The company offers its own AI models, but they're less popular than leading models from OpenAI and Anthropic and aren't at the forefront in terms of performance, according to one benchmark . Developers are more likely to have used alternatives, according to a recent survey . This isn't the first time Microsoft has sought to use the AI boom as a way to boost sales of its devices. In 2024, the company introduced the Copilot+ PC standard, requiring the inclusion of neural processing units that ensure a minimum level of AI performance, along with compliant Surface computers. But Microsoft has since "simplified product naming to lead with the Surface brand, while continuing to deliver premium hardware and hybrid AI experiences," a spokesperson said. The new device sports a 15-inch display and weighs 4.4 pounds. It can contain up to 128 gigabytes of unified memory and supply up to one petaflop of computing power. The Blackwell RTX Spark GPU inside the computer has as much processing power as Nvidia's DGX-1 data center server from 2016, which cost $250 million, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said at Wednesday's event. A presenter showed how apps on the Surface Laptop Ultra can route some AI coding requests run on the computer's local GPU, displaying a green leaf icon, and others to the cloud. Through Windows 11, developers can confine coding agents to Microsoft Execution Containers that will prevent unwanted system access. Microsoft is updating its Windows 11 device setup experience to help people get started quickly with open-source OpenClaw AI agent software. Microsoft has been releasing its own computers since 2012, and CEO Satya Nadella indicated on Tuesday that the company's position in the market is evolving. "I think today is the day we'll start talking and thinking about the frontier ecosystem taking maybe slightly different contours two years from now, five years from now, 10 years from now," Nadella said at the event. "That classic edge that distributed computing will always remain distributed will be more true." headlines.summary: Since SpaceX's record-breaking IPO in June, rates have sold off, and yields on its bonds have risen, along with other AI-related bonds.
headlines.article_text: SpaceX in talks with Apollo, banks to back $40B Nvidia chip buy Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Apollo Capital and several banks are in talks with SpaceX to facilitate the $40 billion purchase of Nvidia GPUs, a source told CNBC. The deal will primarily rely on the investment-grade debt market. Discussions are preliminary and details have yet to be finalized, including key lenders. In this article SPCX NVDA APO Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 2:13 02:13 SpaceX in talks with Apollo, consortium of banks to support $40 billion purchase of Nvidia GPUs Squawk on the Street Apollo Capital Management and several banks are in discussions with SpaceX to help facilitate the company's purchase of $40 billion worth of Nvidia graphics processing units, according to a person familiar with the talks who asked not to be named to discuss the matter. The deal will primarily rely on the investment-grade debt market, which SpaceX just tapped four months ago, the person said. Two weeks after its record-breaking IPO in mid-June, the space exploration company raised $25 billion in bonds at different durations. CNBC was told at the time that SpaceX's bond sale saw incredibly high demand, highlighting strong interest from fixed-income investors. But since then, artificial intelligence-related bonds have sold off, while credit spreads have widened. SpaceX's $40 billion debt deal will likely use GPUs as collateral and Apollo Capital is said to be playing a leading role in facilitating the financing, the person said. Apollo declined to comment. Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The market is still operating under the expectation that GPUs hold their value for about seven years, according to a person in the credit industry who asked not to be named to discuss the matter. Computing power is scarce and the shortage is not expected to abate anytime soon, which supports the value of high-performing GPUs. The Financial Times was first to report on the financing talks. Both sources told CNBC that more debt sales are expected, fixed-income investors are demanding a higher yield to service the debt, a sign that participants are becoming more selective about their AI exposure. SpaceX is already running a massive load of Nvidia AI chips and has plans to add to it. CEO Elon Musk said in a Sept. 24 post on X that his company's Colossus data center in Memphis, Tenn., was running 230,000 Nvidia AI chips, while Colossus 2 had 550,000. Musk said plans were to more than double the number of chips by late December to reach 1.21 million. For the SpaceX bulls, the company has inked compute deals with Google , Anthropic , Cursor and Reflection AI, and bringing more capacity online could boost revenue quickly. On the flipside, the company reported nearly $40 billion in debt in its second-quarter financials, and its existing debt trades near junk bond levels, as credit markets have, overall, been more However, to make SpaceX's ambitions a reality, it needs to keep spending — and on more than just chips. —CNBC's Morgan Brennan contributed to this article watch now VIDEO 4:57 04:57 William Blair’s Louie DiPalma: We estimate SpaceX will spend about $50 billion on AI capex this year Squawk on the Street Choose CNBC as your preferred source on Google and never miss a moment from the most trusted name in business news.

headlines.title: Modelo owner Constellation is getting creative to bring back beer drinkers as overall demand weakens
headlines.summary: Constellation Brands beat earnings and revenue expectations as beer brands gained share, while inventory rebuilding and consumer caution clouded demand.
headlines.article_text: Constellation Brands earnings beat, beer demand slows Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Constellation Brands beat Wall Street's quarterly earnings and revenue expectations. While beer sales rose, underlying indicators of demand showed consumer willingness to spend is still tepid. Constellation is looking to special occasions or events, along with expansion into ready-to-drink cocktails, to counteract slower spending. In this article STZ Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Bottles of Corona beer, the flagship brand of Grupo Modelo are displayed in this illustration taken in Monterrey, Mexico, Feb. 18, 2025. Daniel Becerril | Reuters Constellation Brands beat quarterly earnings and revenue expectations as its beer brands gained market share, but continued consumer caution tempered results. As it navigates high food and fuel prices and choosy shoppers, Constellation is turning to special occasions and diversification to help drive sales. The maker of Modelo Especial, Corona and Pacifico on Tuesday reported fiscal second-quarter adjusted earnings of $3.74 per share on $2.63 billion in revenue, ahead of Wall Street estimates of $3.56 and $2.54 billion, respectively. Beer revenue rose 5% to roughly $2.47 billion, while beer shipments increased 5.5%. However, the company said beer depletions, a measure of sales from distributors to retailers and other customers, declined slightly during the quarter, indicating consumer demand was softer than shipment growth suggests. "We have spent much of the first half rebuilding distributor inventory levels," said Constellation Brands CEO Nicholas Fink on the company's earnings call on Wednesday. "While there is always going to be month-to-month variability, September depletions are trending in the right direction." The broader backdrop remains challenging for beer sellers. U.S. beer sales fell 1.8% year over year in the two weeks ended Sept. 19, according to Nielsen's latest data. Still, Fink said September beer depletions improved even beyond the benefit of a later Labor Day, and that the recovery was broad-based across channels. He said consumers were "across the board" engaging in the category. Some analysts said the results indicated elevated gas prices have dampened Constellation's performance. “Progress [for Constellation] had accelerated to start 2026, but has been derailed by higher fuel costs,” Roth Capital analyst Bill Kirk wrote, though he said Constellation continues to deliver against its fiscal 2027 plan. Kirk has a buy rating and $209 price target on the stock, compared with the roughly $116 a share price as of Wednesday. Fink said Constellation saw particular strength in club stores, which have benefited as cash-strapped shoppers seek deals on fuel and groceries. The company is also working to better tailor its product and pack sizes across channels, as consumers make different choices depending on where they are shopping, and for what occasion. That focus on events also extends to younger drinkers. Fink said consumers are increasingly buying beer for specific moments, rather than treating it as a default purchase, and Constellation is leaning into sports, music, beach activations and other occasions to drive sales. The company's pricing strategy reflects consumer caution around spending. Chief Financial Officer Garth Hankinson said Constellation has been selective with price increases, keeping them at the low end of its usual range given the "macroeconomic backdrop and the impact that that's having on our consumer." Hankinson said it is "much more cost-effective to retain your consumers than it is to try to regain your consumers." That price sensitivity is especially important for Constellation, given its reliance on Hispanic shoppers. About 40% of spending on Constellation's beer comes from Hispanic consumers, compared with roughly 15% for the overall beer category, according to company data. That cohort has faced more economic concerns , including pressure from the labor market and household finances in part fueled by President Donald Trump's policy of mass deportation. Constellation has previously said that beer demand has been weaker in areas with larger Hispanic populations, although it has also pointed to improving trends in some markets. Constellation's canned spirits expansion Constellation is also moving beyond its core beer business. The company announced Tuesday that it would acquire SpikedAde , a spirit-based ready-to-drink beverage brand, for $75 million up front, with up to another $278 million in potential payments tied to future performance. The deal gives Constellation a foothold in a new segment that has drawn more interest from consumers. Fink said the company aims to "remain relevant to our consumers and to our customers," adding that distributors have urged Constellation to get into growing categories beyond beer. Some analysts approved of the move. "We consider the acquisition attractive, giving [Constellation] exposure to the fast-growing RTD subcategory," said Piper Sandler analyst Michael Lavery, who also noted that Stateside Vodka's competing Super Lyte brand has also had "a very strong start" on the East Coast. Lavery has a neutral rating and $161 price target on Constellation's stock. While Fink said beer will remain the company's primary source of value creation, he called SpikedAde a "long, wide-open runway" for Constellation's brand-building and distribution capabilities. According to the Distilled Spirits Council of the United States, sales of premixed cocktails including spirits-based RTDs grew 16.4% in 2025 to $3.8 billion, making them the spirits industry's strongest growth category.
